text:
joel: quick sync — we need a strict apples-to-apples plan for the A vs B perf runs. goal: isolate kernel selection + batching + kv behavior.

maria: agree. main constraints: identical prompts, tokenizer alignment, same decode params, same stop sequences, and identical replay vs synth traffic config.

alex: +1. propose we pin: `seed=42`, `temperature=0.0`, `top_p=1.0`, `max_new_tokens=128`, `stop_tokens=["\n"]`. also force `deterministic=True` in the harness.

joel: sounds good. for kernel selection we should run two modes: runtime-default (auto-kernel) and a forced-kernel path (e.g., `kernel=fast8bit`) so we can see delta. keep batch-sizing policy identical.

kevin: on batching heuristics — let's capture per-request seq-length histogram and feed same seq-distribution into the synthetic driver. if replay harness used, we must normalize pad/truncate rules so token counts equal.

maria: capturing KV cache metrics is critical. add `kv_hits`, `kv_bytes_cached`, `kv_miss_latency` counters in the trace. also record `kv_prefetch` toggles.

alex: I put a minimal config snippet below for the harness. use the same weights (exact model git sha) for both runs and run each mode 3x: warmup + 10k samples for median.

```
# harness snippet
model: open-model:v2@sha=abcdef1234
decode:
  seed: 42
  temperature: 0.0
  top_p: 1.0
  max_new_tokens: 128
  stop_tokens: ["\n"]
traffic:
  mode: replay
  normalize_token_counts: true
  synth_seq_histogram: from_replay
metrics:
  capture: [p99_latency, median_latency, tokens_per_sec, kv_hits, kv_miss_latency, cpu_gpu_util]
runs: 3
warmup: 1000
```

joel: nice. small checklist: 1) tokenizer parity check (same vocab/tokenizer args + run tokenized sample diff), 2) exact decode params, 3) model binary sha pinned, 4) identical traffic shape, 5) kernel forced vs auto, 6) collect base traces + perf counters.

perf-bot: scheduled run `1715008923-A-vs-B-control` queued on cluster `dedicated-pool-3` (ETA ~10m) :rocket:

kevin: i'll wire the KV counters into the runtime traces and start the replay normalizer. will post run links when done.

maria: when results land, we should run a quick regression script that diffs token-level outputs for a sample of 200 prompts to ensure no output-quality drift (stop seq alignment + tokenizer mismatch can silently alter results).

joel: perfect. thanks team — keep the thread updated with links to the run artifacts and any anomalies (e.g., decoding divergence or weird tokenization diffs).
